Gear and Wear Cubes These cubes are the same every game. 3rd Gear (White) - These allow you to move onto a white space on the board. 4th Gear (Light Gray) - These allow you to move onto a light gray space on the board. The light gray spaces are typically longer than white spaces, so these are more powerful than 3rd Gear cubes. 5th Gear (Dark Gray) - These allow you to move onto a dark gray space on the board. The dark gray spaces are typically longer than white and light gray spaces, so these are more powerful than 3rd and 4th Gear cubes. 6th Gear (Black) - These allow you to move onto a black space on the board. The black spaces are the longest, so these are the most powerful cube. Wear (Brown) - These cubes are useless! They perform no function and every one that you draw is one less useful cube that you've missed out on. Powerful cards and travelling at high speed will gain you wear, so you will need to take steps to keep removing it or you may become overwhelmed! Other Cubes The other 5 cubes may perform different actions each game. In each game a card is used to determine the function of each cube colour, and playing a cube will perform the action on the card of the same colour. The cards used in a game can come from a pre-chosen set or it can be random. Garage (Yellow) - Garage cards are generally used to manage your cube supply. [Rating: 2/10] Unplayable for colourblind gamers, Very bad indeed - I found it completely impossible, even with significant assistance. Many pieces need to be swapped out for this to be fixed.

[Rating: 3/10] This is a bad bag building game. No tension, very dry. you may be stuck due to a bad draw. Avoid.

[Rating: 3/10] This is a bag building game about racing cars. It uses the game concept that the faster you are going, the more brown cubes you get, which clog up your future bag pulls. This can be avoided if you pull up right behind someone, so it seems like it's meant to balance the leader. The problem with this is if one player gets a bad turn or two in a row due to luck of their draws, the player in the lead can lap and follow the player in last, thereby removing what should be their penalty for being first, while the player in last is taking brown cubes with each move as they can't catch up to the next p

[Rating: 3/10] At least based on Yucata play, didn't do anything for me. Feels like cube management, not racing.

[Rating: 3/10] Racing games are better if turns are quicker - feels more like stop motion animation than a race.

[Rating: 3/10] It is many things but it is not motor racing. One of the poorest mixes of theme and mechanics I have seen.

[Rating: 3/10] Im not a fan of racing games nor deck builders. No surprise I didn't like this one. I guess it comes down to the lack of opportunity of strategic planning in the game.  But I could recommend it to other that like games like Flamme Rouge or even Clank!

[Rating: 3/10] I find the cube management and powers to be tedious. Vastly prefer the streamlined simplicity of Quest for El Dorado.

[Rating: 4/10] A light bag builder that I didn't find very captivating. Mechanically I'd rather play something like Orleans and thematically I'd rather play Formula D.
